description: Open a URL as a hidden Staging page with the user's profile: a page you may take Panels from, or one your own tools can't read properly. Find which pages to open with your own search; Banquish has no search. It waits for the page to settle (up to about 10 s), and you get the outline of its Candidate tree: the meaningful parts of the page, largest sections opened first, in at most 40 lines. The result holds the page id and the lines, each one string per candidate: `[id] ^parent kinds tag#htmlId.classes[role=…][aria="label"] @x,y wxh | counts | h:"heading" | "text" | +k`. ^parent is the candidate it sits in (^- for none); kinds are list:N (N items), item, ctl (a control), scrolls:H, fixed, or range a-b of n (a slice of a long level); @x,y wxh is its box on the page in CSS px; counts are the images, media, buttons, inputs and links inside it, left out when none; h: is its heading and "text" the start of its text; +k counts candidates inside it not shown. The result says if the page still shows a loading screen, and names the HTTP status when the page answered with an error (400 or above). Use expand and find to see more, as the page is then; ids stay valid while their candidates are on the page. Only your few most recently used pages keep running: one you leave behind (or unused for a few minutes) is unloaded to save memory and opened again when you next use it, keeping the ids of what's still in the same place. Pages on the user's Private sites are refused.
name: open_page
